newsitem.title: UK: UK turns down proposed visit by Iraqi oil officials.
newsitem.headline: UK turns down proposed visit by Iraqi oil officials.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it would not allow a visit by a delegation from the Iraqi oil ministry, just a day after saying the proposed trip would go ahead.

An official said Britain had turned down visa applications from five Iraqi officials who planned to hold talks on selling oil for food and medicines as part of a deal approved by the U.N. Security Council.
The foreign ministry official, speaking by telephone, said Britain had not changed its policy of barring visits by Iraqi officials.
"It is quite legitimate for British companies holding licences to deal with Iraq to speak to Iraqi businessman. But British policy is to reject applications from Iraqi officials," he said.
On Monday another official said the delegation included the director generals of the oil ministry's finance and distribution departments.

The current six-month oil-for-food deal calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from U.N. trade sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
About two-thirds of the money is for humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
